declarations.doc:
NOTE on `totalDeposited`: it is NET collateral flow and may be negative once a
trader withdraws realised profit, so it carries no sign bound.  It is read by
`inv_conservation`, which is the property it exists for.
T3 for this protocol, half one (P2-SCOPE §5 row 7, `inv_impactSign`): the pool
is never negative and never exceeds the balance backing it.  Both halves are
consequences of `capPositiveImpact`, which v1 has no occasion to state because
nothing ever pays out of the pool.
declarations.name: inv_impactPoolBacked

declarations.doc:
`validateReserve` is a real bound: open interest is covered by the pool at the
configured reserve factor at the moment every order is accepted.  v1's version
of this line dropped `reserveFactor`, so its bound was 2.5x looser.
declarations.name: inv_reserveFactorLive

declarations.doc:
T0-LIVE for this protocol: `sameSide(30000, 20000) = +250`, as a TRACE.
The pool was filled to 45 tokens by the charge for opening 30000 of long
against nothing, and the 10000 short that narrowed the imbalance from 30000 to
20000 was rebated exactly 250 USD, i.e. 25 tokens.  Under the linearised
mutant the same two orders give a charge of 150 and a rebate of 50, so the
pool holds 10 and `lastImpactUsd` is 50 — this state is unreachable, which is
exactly how a value-level equality becomes a mechanism check.
declarations.name: wit_live_convexImpact

declarations.doc:
`impactUsd` ran and CHARGED: the pool holds tokens that only a negative price
impact can have put there.  Tag-free — under v1 the pool is fed by liquidation
residue and by nothing else, which is contrast member M3.
declarations.name: wit_used_impactUsd

declarations.doc:
`capPositiveImpact` ran on the REBATE side: the pool paid out, so it fell
while open interest was still open.
declarations.name: wit_used_capPositiveImpact

declarations.doc: 6f: the cap BOUND — a rebate was clipped to what the pool could pay.

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: wit_branch_crossover

declarations.doc:

declarations.doc:
CONSERVATION — index tokens are neither created nor destroyed.  Every token in
the market is either LP-owned (`poolAmount`, of which `impactPool` is a
sub-balance, MarketUtils.sol:1085-1130) or a trader's collateral, and the total
moves only by deposits and withdrawals.  This is the T2 command's invariant,
and it is reported for the reason the pilot reported its own: it holds under
the linearised mutant too, so it is evidence of nothing about the mechanism.
declarations.name: inv_conservation

declarations.doc:
T3 for this protocol, half two, and THE INVARIANT THAT KILLS THE MUTANT.
CONVEXITY, stated over the declared imbalance domain: equal steps of the
imbalance cost strictly MORE the further out they start.  Every linear impact
function makes the two sides equal and violates it.  Evaluated at the live
market configuration rather than at constants.
declarations.name: inv_impactConvex

the comparison of the two impacts rather than of the two imbalances — which is
the anti-gaming clause the comment at PositionPricingUtils.sol:204-208 explains.

branch even though the imbalance only grew.  M4 gets this one wrong.

but measured on opposite sides) and the charge is f(10000) - f(20000).

declarations.doc:
Convention 6 / 6g: every `nondet` is exogenous — an order field or an oracle
return.  The IMPACT is not among them: it is computed from `longOI`, `shortOI`
and the order size, which is the dependency v1 had no quantity to carry.
declarations.name: step

declarations.doc:
Exact floor(sqrt(n)) for 0 <= n < 4^bits.
`bits` fold steps; each step is one multiply and one compare.
Largest intermediate is (2^bits)^2 = 4^bits, so pick `bits` so that
4^bits fits the backend integer width (Rust backend: bits <= 31).
declarations.name: isqrtBits

declarations.doc: TypeScript backend (BigInt): exact on 0 <= n < 2^128.
declarations.name: isqrtWide

declarations.doc: Defining property of floor(sqrt).
declarations.name: isqrtCorrect

declarations.doc: Quint Rust-backend integer ceiling.  Every `BOUNDS:` peak must be below it.
declarations.name: I64_MAX

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:76 specialised to the 2-coin pool (P2-SCOPE row 2
permits the 3 -> 2 reduction).
declarations.name: NEWTON_N

declarations.doc: Unrolling depth of the `for _i in range(255)` loop.  See the note above.
declarations.name: NEWTON_K

declarations.doc:
The loop carriage: the current iterate, the previous one (the contract's
`Dprev`), whether the contract's `break` has fired, and the real iteration
count.  `v`/`vprev` are read by `newtonBreak`, `done` and `iters` by
`kernelNewtonOk` and by every caller's convergence obligation.
declarations.name: NewtonState

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:211-217, verbatim, including the branch on direction:
  if D > Dprev:  if D - Dprev <= 1: break
  else:          if Dprev - D <= 1: break
declarations.name: newtonBreak

declarations.doc: Signed magnitude.  Needed by every spec that carries a signed position.
declarations.name: absInt

declarations.doc:
`isqrtFloor` — exact floor(sqrt(n)) on 0 <= n < 2^62, 31 restoring folds.
Verified at gate 2.0d on ~14k points; see `kernelSqrtVerified`.
Peak intermediate inside the fold: (2^31 - 1)^2 = 4.611686e18 < I64_MAX.
Models `Math.sqrt` (Uniswap_v2-core/contracts/libraries/Math.sol:11-20),
whose Babylonian loop returns the same exact floor for every uint.
declarations.name: isqrtFloor

declarations.doc: The defining property of floor(sqrt), for use in `inv_sqrtExact`.
declarations.name: isqrtExactAt

declarations.doc:
Take one step to `vNew` and evaluate the contract's break condition on the
pair (new, previous).  Every Newton loop in the corpus goes through here.
declarations.name: newtonAdvance

declarations.doc:
One iteration of StableSwap3Pool.vy:206-210, same rounding, same order:
  D_P = D*D/(x*N) ; D_P = D_P*D/(y*N)
  D   = (Ann*S + D_P*N)*D / ((Ann-1)*D + (N+1)*D_P)
Once `done` the accumulator is the identity, which is what `break` means.
declarations.name: newtonDStep

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:195-218 for N = 2, unrolled to `maxIter`.
`S == 0` returns 0 (:199-200); a zero balance is the contract's own
division-by-zero case (:208 comment, "only withdrawal will work"), so it is
returned as 0 with the loop never entered.
declarations.name: newtonDFull

declarations.doc: The value the contract returns.  Callers MUST also assert `newtonDConverged`.
declarations.name: newtonD

declarations.doc:
The proof obligation the unrolling exports: the loop terminated the way the
contract's `break` would.  False means K is too small AT THIS POINT and the
returned D is not the contract's D.
declarations.name: newtonDConverged

declarations.doc: The real iteration count, i.e. how many times the contract's loop body ran.
declarations.name: newtonDIters

declarations.doc:
|D_next - D| at the returned D: the residual of the fixpoint equation the
iteration solves.  `<= 1` is the contract's own tolerance (:211-217).
declarations.name: newtonDResidual

Convention 6 / 6g: every `nondet` is exogenous — an order field or an oracle
return.  The IMPACT is not among them: it is computed from `longOI`, `shortOI`

1563.doc:
CONSERVATION — index tokens are neither created nor destroyed.  Every token in
the market is either LP-owned (`poolAmount`, of which `impactPool` is a
sub-balance, MarketUtils.sol:1085-1130) or a trader's collateral, and the total
moves only by deposits and withdrawals.  This is the T2 command's invariant,
and it is reported for the reason the pilot reported its own: it holds under
the linearised mutant too, so it is evidence of nothing about the mechanism.
1563.name: inv_conservation

1614.doc:

trader withdraws realised profit, so it carries no sign bound.  It is read by
`inv_conservation`, which is the property it exists for.
T3 for this protocol, half one (P2-SCOPE §5 row 7, `inv_impactSign`): the pool
is never negative and never exceeds the balance backing it.  Both halves are
consequences of `capPositiveImpact`, which v1 has no occasion to state because
nothing ever pays out of the pool.
1614.name: inv_impactPoolBacked

1727.doc:
T0-LIVE for this protocol: `sameSide(30000, 20000) = +250`, as a TRACE.
The pool was filled to 45 tokens by the charge for opening 30000 of long
against nothing, and the 10000 short that narrowed the imbalance from 30000 to
20000 was rebated exactly 250 USD, i.e. 25 tokens.  Under the linearised
mutant the same two orders give a charge of 150 and a rebate of 50, so the
pool holds 10 and `lastImpactUsd` is 50 — this state is unreachable, which is
exactly how a value-level equality becomes a mechanism check.
